title: Grainline research log — weekly capture (2028-08-22)
content:
Purpose:
Capture the week: quick wins, regressions, and tasks for compact model onboarding and quantization experiments. Focus this week on three threads: 1) 4-bit AWQ vs GPTQ on nova-7b-compact; 2) eval harness drift on instruction-following testset; 3) model onboarding checklist friction (tokenizer + runtime flags).

Highlights (TL;DR):
- AWQ 4-bit run looks promising for latency/cost but shows an instruction-following drop (~6% accuracy delta on our prefer-testset).
- GPTQ-4 baseline has slightly better instruction alignment but higher memory pressure leading to increased tail latency on microbatch sizes >8.
- Found a tokenizer edge (unicode normalization mismatch) when onboarding open-nova-v2 which produced bad prompt truncation in 0.7% of requests — tracked to token-to-byte mapping change in new tokenizer release.
- KV-cache prefetch patch reduced cold-start tail by ~22ms on p4d-24 clusters.

Experiments run this week (short notes):
- experiment/awq-nova7b-4bit-aug18: AWQ quantization with per-channel scales. 3 seeds, eval on prefer-testset (2.5k examples). Mean latency (microbatch=4): 85ms/token; p95 132ms/token. Instr-acc: 78.4% (baseline fp16: 84.1%). Notes: hallucination rate unchanged; calibration suggests small bias in end-of-answer token probabilities.
- experiment/gptq-nova7b-4bit-aug19: GPTQ-4k chunking, kernel-level fuse enabled. Latency (mb4): 98ms/token; p95 150ms. Instr-acc: 81.7%. OOMs observed on mb16/seq2048.
- experiment/kv-prefetch-patch-a: runtime change that warms prefix KV into GPU before decode. Reduced cold-start requests by median 22ms, p99 improved by ~18ms. No correctness impact.
- experiment/tokenizer-normalize-check: compared BPE variants; found open-nova-v2 tokenizer default uses NFKC normalization while our serving pipeline expects NFC -> mismatch on some multi-byte symbols. Patch proposal attached.

Key observations and interpretations:
- AWQ gives better throughput and lower memory footprint which is attractive for Dedicated/Dedicated-Low tiers. However there is a measurable drop in instruction-following accuracy on long-context turns. Hypothesis: AWQ per-channel scale + sym quantization interacts with attention softmax scale when softmax inputs have long-tailed logits for instruction markers. Need targeted probing.
- GPTQ remains the safer default for quality-sensitive customers but needs memory-pressure handling: either smaller microbatch (but impacts throughput) or staged KV offload.
- Tokenizer mismatch is low-frequency but customer-visible — onboarding checklist should require tokenizer equality check (hash of tokenizer config and sample-echo test) as gating step.

Action items (owners & dates):
- Priya: run AWQ tuning sweep focusing on end-of-answer bias calibration (temperature-aware scale comp) and produce delta report. Due 2028-08-30.
- Samir: add tokenizer equality check to onboarding checklist + small test harness that echoes back tokenization for 50 synthetic edge prompts. PR: GH link -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/85. Due 2028-08-24.
- Lena: instrument eval harness to break down instruction-following failures by token-length and prompt-type (system vs user). Add per-failure trace ids to linked artifacts. Due 2028-08-29.
- Marco: prototype KV offload shim for GPTQ runs to avoid OOMs at mb>=8 (poc on infra-staging). Due 2028-09-05.
- Diane: run 7-day canary for nova-7b-compact AWQ on Dedicated-Low with slug sampling, surface cost delta and # of regressions. Due 2028-08-28.

Open questions (short):
- Is AWQ instruction drop correlated with specific token IDs (system prompts markers)? Need token-level attribution.
- Can we get a kernel-level quantization trick that preserves the logit-shape for EOS probs? (ask research kernel folks)
- Should onboarding gate require both tokenizer hash and sample-generation equality within tolerance, or is hash enough? (ops vs security tradeoffs)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Try mixing AWQ for feed-forward mats and GPTQ for attention weights (hybrid quantization) — might recover instruction accuracy while keeping memory win.
- Add short unit test to eval harness that runs a micro-sampled 50-case instruction-check on every PR changing quant kernels.

Customer / product context:
- Two mid-market customers asked for 4-bit options to lower running costs. One is OK to accept small accuracy tradeoff; the other requires strict instruction-following. We should prepare two recommended profiles: compact-cost (AWQ tuned) and compact-fidelity (GPTQ + KV offload).

Meeting notes (standup 2028-08-22):
- Quick sync with infra: p4d queue improved after kernel patch; still seeing higher p95 for GPTQ on mb16.
- Product: proposed onboarding checklist change approved in principle; want minimal gate to avoid friction but enough safety for regulators.
- SRE: asked for early-warning alerts on tokenizer changes deployed by infra images. Action: Samir to add to repo-deploy hook.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: AWQ regression unnoticed in long-tail instruction types -> mitigation: expand eval corpus with stratified sampling of system-heavy prompts.
- Risk: OOMs in high-concurrency GPTQ -> mitigation: autoscaler policy + emergency fallback to AWQ variant with known quality delta configured in rollout policy.

Appendix: quick results table (summary numbers):
- fp16 baseline (nova-7b): instr-acc 84.1%, latency mb4 120ms/token, mem 42GB
- GPTQ-4: instr-acc 81.7%, latency mb4 98ms/token, mem 28GB (OOM @ mb16 seq2048)
- AWQ-4: instr-acc 78.4%, latency mb4 85ms/token, mem 20GB

References & links included above; see linked_artifacts for PR/JIRA.

If anything urgent: ping #applied-ml and @pri on Slack.

End of capture.
